claim: Provide a recency view: a query answering what changed in the graph over a given window (new nodes, supersessions, evidence appends, materializations), so concurrent multi-session activity is observable without reading git log on the JSON.

evidence.detail: Second finding of the observation-loop walkthrough, made acute the same day by three sessions writing the repos concurrently. Persisted as a directive per b496. Preflight 2026-06-11: observability tag-overlap with b497 (the lap-log convention, compatible sibling); no semantic conflict.

Live specimen within hours of authoring: a stale-memory directive (paradigm:a367) was minted for an extraction another session had already completed; the observation lap caught it at the READ station. A recency view makes that class of authoring error structurally unlikely rather than vigilance-dependent.

todos.action: Implement mix bs recent [--since DATE | --days N]: deterministic window scan over the loaded graph, events grouped by class (new nodes, supersessions, evidence appends, materializations, retractions); honors --beliefs PATH
Cover and document bs recent: tests for the window scan and each event class, plus the mix bs help entry
